bullets.text: Net loss of $70M—first in 26 years; $1.4B in net realized and OTTI portfolio losses (~10% of invested assets); capital preserved several hundred million above contingency layers; operating cash flow positive 100 consecutive quarters.
CR 94.6 beat 96 target; pretax underwriting income reached $735M; 42 of 50 established states and 8 of top 10 states were profitable, including New York auto; net loss was $70M.

In June, high gas prices coincided with a sudden, dramatic reduction in claims frequency. Later in 2008, consumer behavior lacked perfect elasticity amid economic tailspin, dampening frequency return to first-quarter levels.
Total PIF +3% (+350,000); Direct auto PIF +9% with 4% NPW growth; Agency and Direct auto policy life expectancy both +11%; one month of policy life valued over $1B lifetime premium.
Companywide NPW growth stalled at (1)%, (1)%, and 3% across 1, 3, and 5 years, versus industry 0.5%, <1%, and 1%; Direct new app average premiums lagged prior year by 6%.
Launched "Flo" in superstore-themed TV ad campaign; hired Larry Bloomenkranz as CMO; title-sponsored $10M Progressive Automotive X PRIZE to inspire viable, super fuel-efficient vehicles.
Introduced "Name Your Price" quoting option; expanded MyRate UBI across states; expanded Progressive Home Advantage with Homesite to 46 states for Direct and 33 states for Agency.

Claims and IT made substantial progress redesigning operations at lower costs. Concierge centers proved central to the redesigned process architecture. Claims management creatively resolved staffing challenges from reduced claims frequency.
Entered Massachusetts on May 1st, achieving nationwide availability in all 50 states; Agency business lost nonstandard momentum while increasing acceptance for preferred and commercial auto lines.

Modeled external variables like unemployment and uninsured driver rates, but prioritized observing quickly, reducing time to implement rate changes, and iterating rapidly amid an assumption that change is at an all-time high.
